analysis:
Only base-side text of coordinator/store/postgres.go was supplied (no patch hunks, no head-side excerpt), so the specific PR change is not visible. The excerpt shows the migrate() list. It includes cache-routing tables, which are appended at the end: cacheRoutingHoldersDDL, cacheRoutingDemandDDL, cacheRoutingMetaDDL and related index DDL. It also shows a struct field afterCacheRoutingResetMarker and a comment that ResetCacheRoutingState records an in-progress marker. These are likely the touched areas, but the DDL constants and the reset implementation are not included, so I cannot check what they store.

Security-relevant observations in the base text:
- inference_routes.cache_affinity_key is scrubbed by a trigger and a one-time migration, which supports the T-041 mitigation that raw prompt-cache hashes are not persisted.
- The cache routing tables must not persist raw prefix hashes or token IDs, and must not persist non-HMAC identifiers that link accounts. T-041 and SEC-035 cover the scoping and TTFT oracle. A next pass should check whether cacheRoutingHolders and cacheRoutingDemand hold salt-scoped, HMAC-derived keys only. It should also check whether ResetCacheRoutingState correctly purges them.
- Routing evidence tied to the SSD cache epoch is the likely area of change. The T-041 text says per-file eviction no longer rotates the epoch. A reset should not leave stale holders that route across accounts.

No concrete regression is demonstrable from the supplied text. Coverage is limited, so deeper review is needed on the head-side diff and the cache routing DDL and store code.
